Subject: Pilot onboarding – invoice-first ask (no PO for first 60 days)

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the HelixAnalytics team is excited to kick off the 6-week pilot. Procurement at our side needs a short note from Redwood confirming whether we can provisionally run without a PO for the first 60 days and receive invoices instead. The pilot scope is limited (up to $7,500 total) and we can sign a short addendum that references standard T&Cs.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept an invoice-first path for this pilot and, if so, what evidence your finance team will require (insurance, W-9, statement of work, etc.)? We can assemble paperwork quickly.

Attaching a one-page summary of proposed terms.

Thanks,
Claire

Forwarding Helix's request — short pilot, ~$7.5k cap, asking to be invoiced without PO for first 60 days. Internal ask: is there a standard temporary carveout we can grant for small pilots? If yes, what approvals + artifacts do we need to accept invoice-only?

Key constraints:
- We're comfortable with pilots but need to ensure audit trail and risk controls.
- External legal suggests a short addendum referencing master terms.

Requesting Rishi and Kim to advise. Can we handle this as an "invoice-first" pilot (temporary, conditional) and what limits/guardrails should we apply?

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot onboarding – invoice-first ask (no PO for first 60 days)

Sofia / team,

Finance can approve a time-limited invoice-first path for pilots under the following conditions (summary):

1) Dollar cap: total billed amount must be <= $10,000. We recommend setting the pilot cap at $7,500 as Helix proposed.
2) Evidence pack (scanned to vendor record): W-9 (or local tax form), billing contact, corporate insurance certificate, signed pilot addendum referencing Redwood master T&C.
3) Payment terms: Net 30. No automatic renewals — any extension requires PO or formal contract.
4) Approvals: Procurement (Kim) + Finance Ops (Rishi) must both sign off; Legal only if addendum modifies liability or data terms.
5) Accounting coding: revenue must be tagged with temporary pilot GL code; AP must route invoices to the pilot mailbox.
6) Audit controls: we will run an initial sampling of one invoice for validation before paying the first invoice.

Kimberly, can you confirm procurement's side (vendor setup exceptions)? If procurement is fine with the evidence checklist below we can proceed. I'll attach our checklist and a short one-off approval memo for records.

-- Rishi

Attachment: no_po_evidence_checklist.xlsx

Claire / Samir — good news. Finance is willing to approve an invoice-first path for the Helix pilot under a short set of controls. Below is what we need from Helix to get vendor setup and first invoice processing started: 

1) Completed evidence pack (attached checklist) — W-9, billing contact, COI, signed pilot addendum referencing Redwood master terms (one paragraph tying to our master SOW is sufficient).
2) Confirm pilot cap (we will enter $7,500 into the vendor record and block billing above that).
3) Provide the billing email for AP and PO contact (even if PO will not be used during the pilot).

Timeline: if we receive the completed checklist + signed addendum by EOD Friday (14 Nov) we can complete vendor setup and accept the first invoice the following week. We will run a pre-pay sampling review before processing the first payment.

I'll attach the checklist and sample addendum. Once you return those, Kim will create the temporary vendor record and I will send a short approval memo to Finance to close the loop.

Thanks — excited to get this started.
Sofia
